dfs.explain.note: PROJ is the model's fantasy points on Yahoo scoring — its yards, receptions and touchdown rates for this week, half-PPR, for every player it has a rate for and not only the ones a book prices. A player with no game log at all (a rookie) wears a LINE: his own line this week, read as a role. Whoever is left — the deep bench, K, DST — wears a Y: Yahoo's last-season average, rescaled to the model's level at his position, a placeholder rather than a read. No site publishes real ownership before lock — PROJ OWN is a rank-based estimate, same idea any pre-lock ownership projection tool uses.
dfs.explain.step1: Greedy builds the highest-projected lineup — what most of the field lands on. Non-chalk sits the single most-projected play at each position and trades a little projection for a lineup the field isn't all rostering, which is the point of a GPP.
dfs.explain.step2: Swipe the lineups below, tap Load into my lineup to start from one.
dfs.explain.step3: Fill or swap slots from the pool underneath.

parlay.empty.noBest: NO LINE BEATS THE USUAL PRICE HERE
parlay.explain.long: Long slips are 4 or 5 picks from the same legs, priced at the standard board (10× for 4, 20× for 5). A long slip is worth more when every leg is, since the payout grows faster than the chance falls, but Underdog often pays less than the board: type the app's number into your slip and the verdict follows it. Stacks are a QB's passing yards and his team's two biggest receiving-yards lines, all lower, plus one pick from another game. A bad passing day sinks all three together, so they hit together 23.1% of the time in 2025 where three separate legs would hit 13%. Underdog pays less for same-team picks, so a stack needs the app's payout before it says anything.
parlay.explain.note: MODEL % is the chance the over hits, from the player's last 24 games, nudged by what his opponent allows to his position. EDGE is model % minus the book's break-even, in points — +5 means the model likes the over 5 points more than the price needs. Both live behind each line's chevron, not on the card.
parlay.explain.step1: Browse the slips most likely to hit below — on Underdog each card is receptions, TDs, or both, inside one day or kickoff window, and never mixes two days.
parlay.explain.step2: Tap Load into my slip to start from one, or scroll to the lines and tap any player to add a leg yourself.
parlay.explain.step3: Your slip prices itself as you go. Copy slip puts it on the clipboard, ready to type into the book.
parlay.explain.tags: The big number is graded, not the model's raw confidence. A receptions pick counts at the rate picks like it actually hit on 2025's closing lines (57% for a lower at 65%+, 42% for a higher), since the model's confidence ran about 8 points high; a touchdown counts at the model's P(score), which grading found honest. Beats means that chance is at least a quarter over what the payout needs (a 6× slip needs 16.7%, a 3× needs 33.3%). Near is inside that quarter, where a few points either way flips it. Short of means the payout asks for more. One season of grading, so every number here is an estimate.

profile.arch.mean.satellite: The passing-down back: routes over carries.
profile.arch.mean.scrambler: Escapes the pocket; nobody calls it.
profile.arch.mean.situational: Few routes, but used in the red zone.
